title: UploadFile sets default filename = "upload" when posted without filename

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/uploadfile/")
async def create_upload_file(test_file: UploadFile):
	breakpoint()

~~~

def test_empty_file(app, app_client: TestClient, mocker):
    response = app_client.post(ENDPOINT, files={"test_file": b"content"})

-> breakpoint()
(Pdb) test_file
UploadFile(filename='upload', size=7, headers=Headers({'content-disposition': 'form-data; name="test_file"; filename="upload"', 'content-type': 'application/octet-stream'}))
```


### Description

Related to this question: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/10116

In the example above, I thought filename is set to None.
If this is expected behavior, it should be documented in https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/request-files/ or somewhere. 
Also, if filename cannot be empty, `test_file.filename` should not be inferred as `str | None`

I'll be happy to work on this problem in one way or another.

macOS

Chip: Apple M4
MacOS: 15.4.1 (24E263)

### FastAPI Version

0.115.6

### Pydantic Version

2.8.2

### Python Version

3.13.2

_No response_

answer.body:
This comes from `TestClient` (actually, from `httpx` which is used internally in `TestClient`).

Run the following code:

```
import httpx

res = httpx.post(
    "http://localhost:8000/uploadfile/",
    files={"test_file": b"123456"},
)

print(res.request.read())
```

And you will see the request that `httpx` sends:

```
b'--81555b625e6be0c1753b0a563f634b9c\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name="test_file"; filename="upload"\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n\r\n123456\r\n--81555b625e6be0c1753b0a563f634b9c--\r\n'
```

Notice that `filename="upload"` is sent in request.

So, this is not a FastAPI issue
